From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-07T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Preliminary triage: KV cache patterns + batching window observed

Quick triage notes (pre-bridge):
- Observed repeated KV key churn for Velox tenant prefixes leading to frequent evictions (~300 evictions/sec) and spike in cache-miss load to backend. Eviction rate correlates strongly with p95 spikes in the attached dump (kv_cache_dump_06-07.json).
- Batching telemetry shows many single-request batches (batch size=1) during the surge, which increases per-token overhead. Combined with aggressive eviction, this creates HOL blocking: long-tail requests stall hot shards.
- We also see a small subset (~2%) of very long seq requests (seq_len > 250) that amplify kernel time and block hot GPU lanes.

Immediate mitigations we can push (low-risk, reversible):
1) Increase batching window from 4ms -> 8ms (expected p95 improvement, small impact on p50).
2) Enable per-tenant prefix partitioning to reduce KV key collision for Velox (config flag: tenant_prefetch.partitioning=enabled).
3) Temporarily bump Velox quota into a high-priority lane (dedicated burst pool) while we validate changes.
4) Set eviction policy to LRU with longer TTL for Velox's model shards (eviction_ttl_ms: +30000).

If these don’t move the needle, next step is to pre-warm KV entries for known prefixes and increase per-tenant KV cache size (requires infra window, ~2 hours).

I’ve attached kv_cache_dump_06-07.json and a trimmed example of the config patch we’d deploy. I estimate a 20–50% drop in p95 within 30–45 minutes of the first three mitigations.

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv_cache_dump_06-07.json
